class_map.bit_level: one predicted class per flop; 'several' is right only if the truth accepts every kind
class_map.found_vs_verified: found and verified are separate columns everywhere: found is the recognizer's answer matching the register, verified is that match with a structure the harness proved, and every unverified structure carries its verify.py reason bucket
class_map.hold_ceiling: found and verified are reported separately because the harness certifies fewer structures than the recognizer finds. On the development design the gap is the hold obligation: the count condition pins a reload register whose complement is not a bounded set of cubes, so no legal set of VERIFIED cases (the defining case, when_down and the reset cases) covers the space and the hold region cannot be discharged -- and an opaque load case may not be the thing that empties it. This is an ACCEPTED limitation of this freeze, not a recognizer miss and not a contract to widen (lead decision, 2026-09-23).
class_map.lanes_unordered: a shift_register or synchronizer structure with params.lanes_unordered = true is scored within lanes only (its across-lane pairs are counted, not scored)
class_map.lenient_denominators: all registers of the kind (alt_kinds never remove a register)
class_map.lfsr_form: lfsr_crc.form: 'both' matches 'fibonacci', 'galois' and 'both' on either side; 'affine', 'parallel', 'fibonacci' and 'galois' otherwise match only themselves
class_map.params_certification: a compared parameter is CERTIFIED only when the harness VERIFIED the matched structure and named the parameter in the verdict's params_checked; every other compared parameter is TRANSCRIBED -- copied from the recognizer's answer and never checked
class_map.strict_synchronizers: a synchronizer register that is a member of a declared chain unit (a synchronizer unit whose members are all synchronizer registers) is scored strictly through its chain units only
class_map.unit_member_credit: more than half of the member's flops (>= 2 when it has >= 2)

unscored_params.shift_register.direction: RTL index direction (to_msb/to_lsb): the netlist has no RTL indices; the stage order is scored by concordance instead

unverified_reasons.budget: budget: a run budget (conflicts or coverage calls) ran out before the obligation was decided
unverified_reasons.clock domains: clock domains: the structure's flops are not all in one clock domain (root and edge)
unverified_reasons.coverage: coverage: a condition the harness relies on reads the structure's own state and the defining case is not reachable at every own-word value in range
unverified_reasons.form: form: lfsr_crc -- the own-bit matrix is a permutation or is not strongly connected, or an EXPR is not an XOR of the structure's own q's, control.inputs nets and constants
unverified_reasons.hold: hold: control.hold is required for a counter and a shift_register and either was not claimed or the hold region could not be discharged (an opaque load case may not be what empties it)
unverified_reasons.malformed: malformed: the structure does not follow the result schema
unverified_reasons.not checked: not checked: no harness verdict reached the scorer (no netlist, or this run did not verify)
unverified_reasons.order: order: the structure gives no order (the harness builds its templates from it) or order and params disagree
unverified_reasons.params: params: a declared parameter contradicts the structure or the control the harness needs
unverified_reasons.refuted: refuted: a template obligation is FALSE on the netlist; the harness holds a counter-example
unverified_reasons.self-conditioned: self-conditioned: a clock-gating enable reads the structure's own state, which is folded into the next state and which no region can express
unverified_reasons.template: template: a harness-built template does not fit the structure's shape -- the extent and liveness rules (counter width >= 2 with every claimed bit live, shift depth >= 3, synchronizer stages >= 2) or a constant / word-independent template
unverified_reasons.unknown: unknown: a SOLVER LIMIT, not a refutation -- the obligation was neither proved nor refuted
unverified_reasons.unscored kind: unscored kind: not one of the four STRUCTURE_KINDS, so it is never verified
unverified_reasons.unsupported clock: unsupported clock: the harness does not model this flop's clock path, so it proves nothing about it
unverified_reasons.vacuous: vacuous: a named case is unsatisfiable with the reset and async controls inactive, so it would be checked nowhere

out_of_sample.aggregation: one item per structure-kind truth register, except a synchronizer register of a declared chain unit, which is counted through its unit, plus one item per declared structure-kind unit; found = matched a harness-verified structure of an accepted kind at IoU > 0.5; exact = equal flop sets and verified; both libraries pooled (a design contributes twice). This is review[2]'s own aggregation, and the one every published holdout figure has used.
caveats: The corpus is SYNTHETIC and was written by the same project as the recognizer; several of its classes (cohort 2) were added because the generalisation regression set showed them missing (changes.jsonl C23, C31). It is the best out-of-sample estimate that survives this round, not an independent one.

The generalisation regression sets (out/s3/review_generalisation, review_generalisation2) are NO LONGER held out: counter.py, lfsr.py, shift.py, controls.py and verify.py all consulted them (changes.jsonl C25).

TEMPO is the development design: every TEMPO figure is in-sample. Four recognizer fixes were traced from TEMPO misses by truth name (changes.jsonl C27-C30), and PC03, PC06, PC07, PC09, C01-C06, C10 and C21(d) were selected on TEMPO.
These rates come from ONE seeded corpus evaluation; they carry no confidence interval.

They describe the recognizer AND the harness verifier as of source.code_sha256: 'found' means the harness verified the structure, so a change to tools/s3/verify.py moves them as surely as a change to a recognizer module (review[1] issue 2).

THE false_positive_structures COLUMN OVERSTATES; found / exact and their denominators do NOT. out/s3/review_generalisation2/evaluate.py's outcomes() builds its item list from truth registers whose kind is in STRUCTURE_KINDS, so a 'flag' register's alt_kinds are never consulted. Under the truth's TOGGLE_RULE a 1-bit toggle is kind 'flag' with alt_kinds ['counter'] -- the truth EXPLICITLY ACCEPTS a counter over it -- yet such a prediction matches no item there and is scored a false positive. Counted on the evaluation this document was derived from, as false-positive structures of width 1 lying entirely in one truth register of kind 'flag': holdout 2 of 6, train 10 of 16. The overstatement is in the CONSERVATIVE direction. tools/s3/score.py -- the scorer every published table comes from -- does not make this error: score.Truth builds accepts from alt_kinds for EVERY truth register, a flag included. The scoring rule is left as it is on purpose: changing it would move a published out-of-sample number without a lead decision (changes.jsonl T04, T14).
out_of_sample.code_state: every file of OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SOURCES hashes as it did when these rates were derived

source.note: code_sha256 is the FULL hash of every file the evaluation recorded, taken from the tree it still matched when these rates were derived; tools/s3/score.py refuses to quote this document unless every file of score.OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SOURCES still hashes that way, so a later change to the recognizer, verify.py, corpus.py or score.py withholds the estimate instead of ageing it silently (review[1] issues 0-2).

split.rule: tools/s3/corpus.py splits(): per (cohort, family), sha256(name) order, the first (n + 1) // 4 held out, then every corpus.FITTED_ON design forced into train; corpus.DROPPED designs are not in the corpus at all. docs/S3_DESIGN.md section 4.4 states the same rule and the in-sample / out-of-sample protocol.

They describe the recognizer AND the harness verifier as of source.code_sha256: 'found' means the harness verified the structure, so a change to tools/s3/verify.py moves them as surely as a change to a recognizer module (review[1] issue 2).

THE false_positive_structures COLUMN OVERSTATES; found / exact and their denominators do NOT. out/s3/review_generalisation2/evaluate.py's outcomes() builds its item list from truth registers whose kind is in STRUCTURE_KINDS, so a 'flag' register's alt_kinds are never consulted. Under the truth's TOGGLE_RULE a 1-bit toggle is kind 'flag' with alt_kinds ['counter'] -- the truth EXPLICITLY ACCEPTS a counter over it -- yet such a prediction matches no item there and is scored a false positive. Counted on the evaluation this document was derived from, as false-positive structures of width 1 lying entirely in one truth register of kind 'flag': holdout 2 of 6, train 10 of 16. The overstatement is in the CONSERVATIVE direction. tools/s3/score.py -- the scorer every published table comes from -- does not make this error: score.Truth builds accepts from alt_kinds for EVERY truth register, a flag included. The scoring rule is left as it is on purpose: changing it would move a published out-of-sample number without a lead decision (changes.jsonl T04, T14).
